title: More colours
description: Name the colours you have not met yet, and use them with the verb ser.
grammar: adjectives that change, and the words for colours
grammarNote: A colour is an adjective, so it goes straight after the noun it describes: un coche gris.

explanation.summary: Colours are adjectives, and like every other adjective they change their ending to match the thing they describe. Most of them are the same word for men and women.

sections.heading: The colours
sections.body: Gris, turquesa and beis are the same in both genders. Amarillo, marrón, rosa, morado, dorado and claro become amarilla, marrón, rosa, morada, dorada and clara. Rosa is unusual: it does not change at all, and neither does it need an accent.

sections.heading: Where the colour goes
sections.body: A colour goes straight after the noun, with no article: el queso es blanco, la pared es amarilla. When the colour comes first, it takes el or la like an adjective: el café está oscuro, la casa es blanca.

items.note: The same in both genders: un día gris.
The same in both genders: un café marrón.
The same in both genders: una camisa rosa.
The same in both genders: un abrigo beis.
The same in both genders: una camisa turquesa.
The same in both genders: una camisa lila.

drills.note: The colour matches the noun it describes.
Marrón is the same in both genders.
Gris is the same in both genders.
The feminine of claro is clara.
